pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Thallium Toxicity (Thallium Poisoning) THE SMOKING GUN: The triad of severe painful peripheral neuropathy, autonomic/GI dysfunction, and sudden, delayed alopecia (hair loss) occurring approximately two weeks post-exposure, alongside dark tapered pigmentation at the hair roots (Mee's lines on nails appear later). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Thallium ions share a similar ionic radius to potassium and readily substitute for potassium in essential biological processes. Thallium actively enters cells via Na+/K+-ATPase pumps, where it inhibits intracellular potassium-dependent enzymes, disrupts oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria, and avidly binds to sulfhydryl groups on structural proteins. This results in widespread cellular energy depletion, axonal degeneration of peripheral nerves, autonomic dysfunction, and rapid disruption of keratin synthesis in hair follicles.
